integrity: The residual-squaring identity is derived directly. The 2x2 universal bound uses unitary Schur form and is sharp by an explicit Jordan family. The 3x3 obstruction is an explicit nilpotent residual realized by the perfectly conditioned target A=I, with exact two-step termination. The standalone checker replays representative exact identities but does not replace the universal proof.
scientific_limitations: Exact-arithmetic analysis of the classical Newton–Schulz inverse iteration. The universal 2x2 threshold is for the Frobenius residual norm; no all-2x2 spectral-norm threshold is claimed. The 3x3 obstruction allows unrestricted initial approximate inverses and therefore does not describe practical scaled-adjoint initializations that enforce norm contraction.
title: A sharp two-dimensional residual-safety radius and a three-dimensional nilpotent spike for Newton–Schulz inversion
